//: Rules code is where a surviving mutant means a real rule is unverified.
Raise these as the suite gets stronger; lowering one needs a decision entry.
Two files are deliberately not mutated, and the reasons differ:
game-kit/src/ui.ts is type declarations — there is no runtime code in it.
ludo/src/ui/board.ts only sets SVG colours, radii and opacities. Mutating
those yields a board that looks slightly different and behaves the same,
so the tests that would kill them could only restate the constants back.
Every DECISION the board makes lives in geometry.ts and placement.ts,
which are pure, mutated, and near 100%. Keep it that way: if drawing code
starts deciding something, that decision belongs in a mutated module.
